title: Epochal prefetch replayer and priority redistributor
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add new epochal prefetch replayer and priority redistributor for more realistic long-tail reproduction and actionable reports. Includes reporter that surfaces KV cache pressure and recommended prefetch window sizes.
description:
Motivation: reproducing long-tail latency behavior in the wild has been difficult because traces alone don't capture prefetch/priming behavior and cross-frontend priority shifts. This PR introduces an epochal prefetch replayer that replays historical sessions in time-epochs while simulating prefetch priming, background eviction, and prioritized request redistribution across simulated frontends. The goal is to produce repeatable, high-fidelity tail events for regression testing and to surface actionable knobs (prefetch window, eviction resilience, priority redistribution) for the serving runtime and Dedicated autoscaler.

What this change does: 1) Adds a replay engine that groups trace events into epochs (time windows) and runs each epoch with configurable prefetch phases where KV cache priming requests are issued prior to main traffic. Prefetches can be prioritized by key hotness and sequence position. 2) Adds a priority redistributor that simulates cross-front-end weight shifts (e.g., when routing policies change or a host becomes saturated) and injects gradual traffic shifts during an epoch to recreate redistributive tail amplification. 3) Adds a reporter that emits epoch-level snapshots (p50/p95/p99/p999 latency histograms), per-kernel flamepoint markers, prefix-KV hit/miss time series, and a compact recommendation blob with suggested prefetch window sizes and batching thresholds. 4) Provides a small Dockerized harness and example configs for running deterministically in CI or locally.

Why this is unique: existing runners focus on synthetic mixes or sequence-phase fuzzers; this PR emphasizes temporal cohesion (epoch boundaries), explicit prefetch simulation, and redistribution dynamics that we observed in production incidents where tail events correlated with rapid route weight changes. The tool is intended to sit alongside other benchmark-lab runners as an integration-level stress test for the serving runtime and caching strategies.

Checklist (intent-to-merge): - [x] Implementation: replay engine, redistributor, reporter - [x] Unit tests for epoch boundary correctness and prefetch ordering - [x] Integration smoke that runs a 3-epoch replay in CI container - [x] Documentation: bench/README.md and example configs - [x] Performance sanity: reproducible p99 regression on synthetic incident trace

How to run (short): docker build -t epoch-replayer . && docker run --rm -v $PWD/examples:/work/examples epoch-replayer --config /work/examples/prefetch-config.yaml --epochs 3 --seed 42

Related work and references: ENG-4267 (incident triage: redistributive tail amplification), ENG-4299 (kvcache eviction profiling). See bench/configs/prefetch-config.yaml for parameterization.

Test plan and observed numbers: CI runs the smoke replay (3 epochs, 10k sessions) in ~8m on a ci-large runner. Local runs with a synthetic incident trace reproduced a 35% increase in p99 when prefetch window was disabled vs enabled (prefetch window = 200ms used in recommendation). The reporter includes raw histograms and a compact CSV meant for downstream ingestion into the telemetry pipeline.

Rollback/compat: purely additive under bench/; no runtime changes. If the tool causes flakiness in CI the revert is trivial (revert this PR).

Files touched (high-level): bench/replayer/epochal_replayer.go, bench/replayer/prefetch_scheduler.go, bench/reporter/epoch_reporter.py, bench/configs/prefetch-config.yaml, Dockerfile.bench, bench/tests/test_epoch_replayer.go, bench/README.md

Open questions/follow-ups: - Integrate reporter output into perf-canary ingest (next PR) - Add a KV backend adapter to simulate different eviction policies - Run across a small sample of real incident traces and publish a short findings doc
